content: We need to indicate number of C=O groups in the molecule. But we have no description of molecule. Possibly the sample is the one at hand, maybe we need to get IR spectra to see carbonyl stretch, or carbon NMR to see carbonyl carbons. The task is simple: count carbonyl groups. We need to determine from data. We have no SMILES. We can request IR spectra which will show C=O stretch around 1700 cm-1. But that may not give count. Carbon NMR could show carbonyl carbons ~200 ppm. Could count peaks. Use carbon_nmr_spectra tool. That returns a string with peaks. Then count number of peaks in carbonyl region (190-220 ppm). That gives number of carbonyl carbons, which equals number of C=O groups (assuming each carbonyl carbon appears). Use carbon_nmr_spectra.
